**BLOCK — changes requested** on `10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec`: one HIGH and one MED structural finding.

**[HIGH] Text-change dependencies must follow the recipient’s current text and be reevaluated after each effect.**

Evidence: [`layers.rs:8095–8111`](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/engine/src/game/layers.rs#L8095-L8111) computes one dependency graph; [`layers.rs:8690–8724`](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/engine/src/game/layers.rs#L8690-L8724) infers substitution dependencies solely from the word pairs. [`text_substitution.rs:342–375`](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/engine/src/game/text_substitution.rs#L342-L375) freezes that order before rewriting the recipient.

The actual Oracle abilities permit this interaction: [Magical Hack](https://scryfall.com/card/5ed/101/magical-hack) says “replacing all instances of one basic land type with another”; [Crystal Spray](https://scryfall.com/card/inv/50/crystal-spray) allows “one basic land type with another until end of turn.” On an Island, resolve A = Island → Swamp (Magical Hack), B = Forest → Island (Magical Hack), then C = Swamp → Forest (Crystal Spray), with all three effects live during that turn. The fixed word-pair graph creates a three-way loop and uses A,B,C, predicting Forest/green mana. Initially B and C affect no word on this recipient. After A, C applies before B; A,C,B yields Island/blue mana.

Physically verified against this repository’s `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`: CR 613.8a tests whether applying another effect changes “what it does to any of the things it applies to”; CR 613.8b says a dependent effect “waits to apply until just after all of those effects have been applied” and reserves timestamp ordering for an actual dependency loop. CR 613.8c explicitly says: “After each effect is applied, the order of remaining effects is reevaluated”. Structural pair equality cannot establish that recipient-dependent relation.

Please determine dependencies from the current recipient text and select/apply effects one at a time, recomputing the remaining relation. Extend the existing state-aware layer dependency-selection authority rather than adding a parallel fixed graph. Add a production cast/resolve regression for this three-word cycle on an Island and a rules-text recipient; the existing chain and same-from tests do not distinguish this case. Confidence is high from exact-head source and verified Oracle/CR analysis. Assumption: the stated resolution order and no other recipient-changing effect; this consequence has not been reproduced by executing a test.

**[MED] Shared-library card-name candidates break the supported determinization domain.**

Evidence: [`candidates.rs:5595–5604`](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/engine/src/ai_support/candidates.rs#L5595-L5604) reads actual shared-library identities into card-name candidates. [`determinize.rs:101–123`](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/phase-ai/src/determinize.rs#L101-L123) and [179–185](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/phase-ai/src/determinize.rs#L179-L185) resample unpinned opponent hand and shared-library identities together. [`search.rs:2617–2624`](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/phase-ai/src/search.rs#L2617-L2624) rebuilds candidates per sample, while [2554–2563](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/phase-ai/src/search.rs#L2554-L2563) requires every action to appear K times. The final [actual-state contract filter](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/blob/10b758a281b9b29c32c818beef8062dd44df40ec/crates/phase-ai/src/search.rs#L555-L556) can reject a sampled-only name.

[Predict](https://scryfall.com/card/c18/98/predict) begins “Choose a card name, then target player mills a card.” With K > 1, an unobserved name whose remaining copies move between opponent hand and the shared library appears in only some sample domains. Source analysis predicts an `observed == K` debug assertion, or a release choice filtered to `None` when absent from the actual-state contract. The new card-name fixture does not combine this path with determinization. Default shipped difficulty configurations currently use K = 0; that limits default exposure but does not fix the supported opt-in sampling path.

Please derive a stable candidate domain from sanctioned deck-pool/known public information, preserving the same issued domain across sampled worlds and the actual contract. Add a Predict regression with an unobserved two-copy name redistributed between opponent hand and the shared library under K > 1; assert constant candidate support and an issued returned action. Confidence is high for the source-level contract mismatch; the assertion/`None` outcomes are predictions, not executed failures. A fixed root domain or pinning all domain-bearing identities would contradict the finding; neither exists in this path.

The independent review covered the full 198-file production scope despite the CLI/bot file cap. The [current-head parse diff](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/pull/9669#issuecomment-6041496799) and immutable artifact `11493462092` from run `37642872708` reconcile to nine claimed cards, six signatures, and no Oracle changes or unexplained parse blast radius. Required CI is green at inspection; it does not exercise the distinguishing cases above. No direct builds/tests or source edits were performed in this review. These shared-layer/AI structural changes need checkpointed implementation and fresh committed-head review before approval; routine maintainer ports caused by main churn remain maintainer work.
